5.criterion: Secondary function reduced; rework of part of the lot.

4.criterion: Appearance or noise bothers most customers; in-line rework.

2.criterion: Only attentive customers notice; minor process disruption.

10.criterion: No prevention control; the failure is practically certain.

9.criterion: Prevention barely effective; the failure occurs very often.

8.criterion: Prevention of little effect; the failure occurs often.

7.criterion: Prevention of limited effect; the failure recurs.

6.criterion: Prevention partly effective; the failure occurs occasionally.

5.criterion: Prevention effective; the failure occurs sporadically.

4.criterion: Prevention effective and proven; the failure is rare.

3.criterion: Proven prevention; the failure is very rare.

2.criterion: Prevention per proven standard; isolated cases only.

1.criterion: Failure prevented by design of the process, e.g. poka-yoke.

10.criterion: No inspection in place or inspection unsuitable.

8.criterion: Effectiveness of the inspection method not proven.

7.criterion: Manual visual or audible inspection, of limited reliability.

6.criterion: Manual inspection with aids, e.g. a gauge.

5.criterion: Proven manual or machine inspection after the process step.

4.criterion: Automatic inspection downstream; the defective part is rejected.

3.criterion: Automatic inspection in the process step; the defective part is rejected.

2.criterion: The cause is detected automatically; no defective part is made.

1.criterion: The failure cannot occur or is always detected.

10.criterion: Safe operation impaired; danger to people.

9.criterion: Product does not meet legal or regulatory requirements.

8.criterion: Product unusable for its intended purpose.

4.criterion: Appearance, noise or feel bothers most customers.

3.criterion: Appearance, noise or feel bothers many customers.

2.criterion: Only a few attentive customers notice.

10.criterion: New technology without experience; no prevention.

9.criterion: First use of a new design; prevention not aimed at the requirement.

8.criterion: New design based on similar technology; little experience.

7.criterion: Known design in a new application.

5.criterion: Carry-over with changes; prevention partly proven.

3.criterion: Minor change to a proven design; prevention tested.

10.criterion: No test or inspection method in place.

9.criterion: Test method not designed for this failure.

7.criterion: Proven method; test only after production release.

6.criterion: Proven method before production release; pass/fail test.

5.criterion: Proven method before production release; test to failure.

4.criterion: Proven method before production release; degradation test.

3.criterion: Proven method early in development; pass/fail test.

2.criterion: Proven method early in development; test to failure or degradation.

1.criterion: Failure excluded or always detected by the method.

fmea.effectPlaceholder: What happens if the failure occurs?
fmea.controlPlaceholder: How is the failure or its cause detected?
fmea.justificationPlaceholder: Why is no action taken for AP H?
fmea.tipS: Severity – How severe is the effect of the failure on the customer? (1 = none, 10 = critical)
fmea.tipO: Occurrence – How likely is it that the failure occurs? (1 = unlikely, 10 = very frequent)
fmea.tipD: Detection – How likely is it that the failure is detected before delivery? (1 = certain, 10 = almost impossible)
fmea.sevHighDesc: Customer strongly affected, function severely limited
fmea.burndownNoData: No rated risks with dated actions available.
fmea.whenToUse: When a process or a design should be surveyed systematically for what can go wrong, what effect it has, how often it occurs and how reliably it is detected — rated by action priority (AIAG-VDA) or risk priority number, with actions and their effect on the rating; not for collecting possible causes without rating them, that is what Ishikawa and the cause-and-effect matrix are for.

setMethod.help: Selects the rating method of the FMEA: AP (action priority per AIAG-VDA) or RPN (risk priority number = severity × occurrence × detection).

params.m: The method: ap rates by action priority (AIAG-VDA), rpn by risk priority number (severity × occurrence × detection). Any other value is an error.

setFmeaType.help: Sets the type of the FMEA; it selects the action-priority scale texts.

params.type: The type: process for a process FMEA, design for a design FMEA. Any other value is an error.

addRisk.help: Adds an empty risk and returns its id.

removeRisk.help: Removes a risk with its actions.

params.id: The id of the risk as read() lists it under risks. An unknown id is an error.

resetScales.help: Discards all custom scale texts; the shipped ones apply again.

sortByPriority.help: Sorts the risks by the active rating method, the most urgent first.

setScaleValue.help: Sets a custom scale text; it replaces the shipped one.

params.key: The key of the scale cell. For the risk priority number these are sevNone, sevNoneDesc, sevLow, sevLowDesc, sevMod, sevModDesc, sevHigh, sevHighDesc, sevVHigh, sevVHighDesc, occUnlikely, occUnlikelyRate, occLow, occLowRate, occMod, occModRate, occHigh, occHighRate, occVHigh, occVHighRate, detCertain, detCertainDesc, detHigh, detHighDesc, detMod, detModDesc, detLow, detLowDesc, detVLow and detVLowDesc; for the action priority ap.<type>.<dimension>.<level>.meaning or .criterion with type process or design, dimension sev, occ or det and level 1 to 10. Any other key is an error.
params.text: The new text. An empty string leaves the cell empty; a missing argument is an error.

setRiskValue.help: Sets one field of a risk.

params.riskId: The id of the risk as read() lists it under risks. An unknown id is an error.
params.field: Which field; each is described individually under keys. Any other value is an error.
params.value: The value; type and allowed range per field are given under keys.

addRiskAction.help: Appends an empty action to the risk; it then sits as the last row of the actions table. The position of the new action, starting at 0, is the return value.

params.riskId: The id of the risk. An unknown id is an error.

removeRiskAction.help: Removes one action of a risk.

params.riskId: The id of the risk. An unknown id is an error.
params.actionIndex: The position of the action in actions, starting at 0. A position where the risk has no action is an error.

setActionValue.help: Sets one field of an action.

params.riskId: The id of the risk. An unknown id is an error.
params.actionIndex: The position of the action in actions, starting at 0. A position where the risk has no action is an error.
params.field: Which field; each is described individually under keys. Any other value is an error.
params.value: The value; type and allowed range per field are given under keys.

risks.help: The risks in working order, each item described under keys. A bulk field: fetch rows via rows.

scales.help: The custom scale texts, one text per scale-cell key; null means the shipped ones apply.

method.help: The rating method: ap by action priority (AIAG-VDA), rpn by risk priority number.

fmeaType.help: The type of the FMEA: process for a process FMEA, design for a design FMEA. It selects the action-priority scale texts.

RiskEntry.id: The id of the risk; use it to address the risk when changing or removing it.
RiskEntry.step: The process step or component under review.
RiskEntry.prevention: The measure that prevents the failure.
RiskEntry.control: The measure that detects the failure.
RiskEntry.specialChar: Special characteristic: CC, SC or empty.
RiskEntry.justification: Why a risk with high action priority stays without a measure.
RiskEntry.sev: Severity as a string 1 to 10, empty while not rated.
RiskEntry.occ: Occurrence as a string 1 to 10, empty while not rated.
RiskEntry.det: Detection as a string 1 to 10, empty while not rated.
RiskEntry.actions: The measures for this risk, each item described under keys.

RiskActionEntry.resp: Who is responsible for the measure.
RiskActionEntry.date: The due date as YYYY-MM-DD, or empty.
RiskActionEntry.deltaS: How much the measure lowers severity, string 0 to 9.
RiskActionEntry.deltaO: How much the measure lowers occurrence, string 0 to 9.
RiskActionEntry.deltaD: How much the measure lowers detection, string 0 to 9.

RiskField.step: The process step or component this risk card examines; free text.
RiskField.failureMode: The potential failure mode: the way in which the step or component can fail at its task. Free text.
RiskField.effect: The potential effect of failure: what the customer or the next process notices of the failure. It drives the severity rating. Free text.
RiskField.cause: The potential cause of failure: why the failure mode occurs. It drives the occurrence rating. Free text.
RiskField.prevention: The prevention control: what stops the cause from occurring in the first place. It feeds into the occurrence rating. Free text.
RiskField.control: The detection control: what detects the failure or its cause before it reaches the customer. It feeds into the detection rating. Free text.
RiskField.specialChar: The special characteristic: CC for a critical, SC for a significant characteristic, empty for none. From a severity of 9 the card points out that it should be checked, while none is set.
RiskField.justification: The justification why a risk with high action priority (H) gets no action. With the AP method the field appears while such a risk has neither an action text nor a justification, and stays visible once filled. Free text.
RiskField.sev: The severity (S) of the failure for the customer, 1 to 10: 1 means no noticeable effect, 10 a safety hazard or regulatory violation; empty means not yet rated. Together with occurrence and detection it gives the priority: with the AP method through the AIAG-VDA handbook table (H, M or L), with RPN as the product severity × occurrence × detection.
RiskField.occ: The occurrence (O), 1 to 10: 1 means the failure is unlikely, 10 that it occurs very frequently; empty means not yet rated. Together with severity and detection it gives the priority (AP table or RPN = severity × occurrence × detection).
RiskField.det: The detection (D), 1 to 10: 1 means the failure is certain to be detected, 10 that it is almost never detected – so a high number is bad; empty means not yet rated. Together with severity and occurrence it gives the priority (AP table or RPN = severity × occurrence × detection).

ActionField.text: The action that is meant to reduce the risk; free text. A risk with high action priority and no action text needs a justification.
ActionField.resp: Who is responsible for the action (Resp.); free text.
ActionField.date: The due date of the action as YYYY-MM-DD; empty means no deadline. Actions with a date form the course in the burndown.
ActionField.done: Whether the action is implemented, yes or no. In the burndown it only then counts toward the actual course.
ActionField.deltaS: By how many levels, 0 to 9, the action is meant to lower the severity. The projection of the risk is severity minus the sum over all its actions, at least 1.
ActionField.deltaO: By how many levels, 0 to 9, the action is meant to lower the occurrence. The projection of the risk is occurrence minus the sum over all its actions, at least 1.
ActionField.deltaD: By how many levels, 0 to 9, the action is meant to lower the detection number, that is improve detection. The projection of the risk is detection minus the sum over all its actions, at least 1.

attribute-test.name: Attribute Tests
attribute-test.description: Tests for proportions, rates and counts: 1 and 2 proportions, Fisher's exact, chi-square association, McNemar, equivalence (TOST), 1 and 2 Poisson rates
attribute-test.ratePooled: Use pooled estimate of the rate for the test
attribute-test.pooled: Use pooled estimate of p for the test
attribute-test.cellLegend: Per cell: observed / expected / contribution to χ²
attribute-test.basisExact: Decision based on the exact binomial test
attribute-test.basisPearson: Decision based on Pearson χ² (two-sided); the direction applies to Fisher's exact test only
attribute-test.h0Assoc: H₀: row and column variable are independent
attribute-test.noteNormalApprox: The normal approximation is not suitable here (n·p₀ or n·(1 − p₀) < 5, or x = 0 or x = n). Use the exact test.
attribute-test.notePooled: The z-test uses the pooled estimate of p; the confidence interval stays unpooled.
attribute-test.warnExpectedBelow1: At least one expected count is below 1 – the χ² test is unreliable.
attribute-test.warnShareBelow5: {share} % of the expected counts are below 5 (more than 20 %) – the χ² test is unreliable.
attribute-test.hintEnterCounts: Enter counts to run the test.
attribute-test.hintPickColumns: Select columns to run the test.
attribute-test.errXGreaterN: The number of events must not exceed n.
attribute-test.errP0Range: p₀ must lie strictly between 0 and 1.
attribute-test.errResponseLevels: The response column needs exactly 2 distinct values.
attribute-test.errGroupLevels: The group column needs exactly 2 levels.
attribute-test.errTableTooSmall: The table needs at least 2 × 2 cells with observations.
attribute-test.statDiscordant: Discordant pairs (event → no event / no event → event)
attribute-test.basisExactPoisson: Decision based on the exact Poisson test
attribute-test.basisZRate: Decision based on the z-test for the rate difference
attribute-test.basisExactMcNemar: Decision based on the exact McNemar test
attribute-test.basisTost: Decision based on two one-sided tests (TOST) against the equivalence bounds
attribute-test.h0McNemar: H₀: the proportion is the same before and after
attribute-test.h0McNemarLabeled: H₀: the proportion is the same for {before} and {after}
attribute-test.noteRatePooledIgnored: With a hypothesized difference ≠ 0 the test runs without the pooled rate.
attribute-test.h0Equiv: H₀: Δ ≤ lower bound or Δ ≥ upper bound (Δ = p₁ − p₂, or p − p₀ for one sample)
attribute-test.h1Equiv: H₁: lower bound < Δ < upper bound
attribute-test.noteRateNormalApprox: The normal approximation is not suitable here (λ₀·t < 5). Use the exact test.
attribute-test.noteNoDiscordant: No discordant pairs – there is nothing to test.
attribute-test.noteSmallDiscordant: Fewer than 10 discordant pairs – use the exact p-value, not the χ² approximation.
attribute-test.noteEquivDegenerate: Both proportions are 0 (or both 1) – the normal approximation cannot be used, so there is no equivalence result.
attribute-test.noteNotEquivalentIsNotEqual: No significant difference does not mean that the proportions are equivalent. Whether the difference is small enough is shown by the equivalence test.
attribute-test.notePairedUseMcNemar: Were the same units inspected before and after? Then McNemar's test is the right one.
attribute-test.noteEquivBoundsPractical: The equivalence bounds are a practical decision, not a statistical one. Fix them before looking at the data.
attribute-test.noteEquivCiOutside: The confidence interval does not lie entirely within the equivalence bounds.
attribute-test.errExposure: Exposure must be a number greater than 0.
attribute-test.errLambda0: The hypothesized rate λ₀ must be greater than 0.
attribute-test.errDiff0: The hypothesized difference must be a number.
attribute-test.errPairsLength: The before and after columns must have the same length.
attribute-test.errPairLevels: Both columns together need exactly 2 distinct values.
attribute-test.hintEnterBounds: Enter the equivalence bounds. They are a practical decision, not a statistical one: which difference would still count as equivalent in practice? Fix them before looking at the data.
attribute-test.errBoundsContainOne: The bounds must enclose 0 (lower < 0 < upper); they apply relative to the target p₀.
attribute-test.deltaOne: Equivalence margin δ (pp, relative to p₀)
attribute-test.noteRateNotTestable: There are no events in either sample, yet the difference is to be tested against a value other than 0 – nothing can be tested.
attribute-test.errBoundsOrder: The lower bound must be smaller than the upper bound.
attribute-test.whenToUse: When counts of events are compared: tests one proportion against a hypothesized value, two proportions against each other (z test and Fisher's exact test), the equivalence of proportions (TOST), paired proportions before and after (McNemar), one or two Poisson rates (events per exposure) or the association of two categorical variables (chi-square on a cross table). The counts are given as summarized numbers or taken from worksheet columns.

setPairCell.help: Sets a count of the McNemar 2 × 2 table with summarized input: how many pairs were in the given state before and after.

params.value: The count as text, '' clears the cell.

checkEquivalence.help: Switches to the equivalence test with two samples, like the “Check with equivalence test” button below a non-significant two-proportion test. It shares counts and columns with the two-proportion test, so they stay; the equivalence bounds stay unchanged.

read.help: Returns the entered configuration, the keys and roles valid in the current state, the selectable columns, the selectable event values and the result. result is null while the inputs are incomplete or invalid; errorMsg then names the reason (an input hint or a refusal such as a too small table) and is empty while a result exists.

params.options: Optional; this module holds no bulk data.

setParam.help: Sets one parameter; the test reruns. Switching testKind or inputMode keeps all other inputs, so switching back loses nothing.

params.key: Which option; each is described individually under keys, the ones allowed in the current state are listed in activeParams. Any other value is an error.
params.value: The value; type and allowed range per key are given under keys. summary values and p0 as text containing a number.

setColumn.help: The data collection column that supplies this role; after a change the analysis is recomputed. If the current event value does not occur in the new response column, its last value counts as the event.

params.slot: One of the roles in activeColumnSlots: response (response column), counts (counts for rates), before and after (McNemar), group, rowVar or colVar.
params.ref: The reference { instanceId, sheetId, columnId } of a column from pickableColumns for that role, or null to clear the role.

setTableCell.help: Sets one count of the cross table used by the association test with summarized input.

params.row: Row index, 0 is the first row.
params.col: Column index, 0 is the first column.
params.value: The count as text, '' clears the cell.

setTableRowName.help: Sets the name of one row of the cross table.

params.row: Row index, 0 is the first row.
params.name: The name as text, '' clears it.

setTableColName.help: Sets the name of one column of the cross table.

params.col: Column index, 0 is the first column.
params.name: The name as text, '' clears it.

addRow.help: Appends a row with empty counts to the cross table; its name is the next letter.

addCol.help: Appends a column with empty counts to the cross table; its name is the next one of X, Y, Z and then C4, C5 and so on.

removeRow.help: Removes one row of the cross table with its counts. Only while the table has more than two rows (at least two remain); otherwise an error.

params.row: Row index, 0 is the first row.

removeCol.help: Removes one column of the cross table with its counts. Only while the table has more than two columns (at least two remain); otherwise an error.

params.col: Column index, 0 is the first column.

runAnalysis.help: Recomputes the test from the current inputs. Missing or invalid inputs are no refusal of the action: result becomes null and errorMsg names the reason.

ratePooled.help: For two rates: true uses the pooled rate for the z statistic, as long as the hypothesized difference is 0.

exposurePerRow.help: The exposure per worksheet row for rates from columns, as entered; the total exposure is the number of rows times this value.

equiv.help: The equivalence test settings: samples (1 or 2), symmetric (true for ±delta), delta, lower and upper as text in percentage points.

testKind.help: The kind of test: 'one' (one proportion), 'two' (two proportions), 'equiv' (equivalence of proportions), 'mcnemar' (paired proportions), 'rate1' (one Poisson rate), 'rate2' (two Poisson rates) or 'assoc' (association in a cross table).

inputMode.help: Where the counts come from: 'summary' (entered numbers) or 'columns' (worksheet columns).

direction.help: The alternative hypothesis: 'two-sided', 'greater' or 'less'. With the association test only active once a result for a 2 x 2 table exists.

alpha.help: The significance level, greater than 0 and less than 1. Starts from the confidence level of the settings.

p0.help: The hypothesized proportion for one proportion, as entered; it must lie between 0 and 1, exclusive.

pooled.help: For two proportions: true uses the pooled standard error for the z statistic.

summary.help: The summarized counts as entered: x and n (one proportion), x1, n1, x2 and n2 (two proportions), t, t1, t2, lambda0 and diff0 (rates), pairs { labels, counts } (McNemar) and table { rows, cols, counts } (association), all as text.

colRefs.help: The chosen column per role: response, counts, before, after, group, rowVar and colVar, each { instanceId, sheetId, columnId } or null.

eventValue.help: The value of the response column that counts as event, or null while there is none.

activeParams.help: The keys setParam accepts in the current state.

activeColumnSlots.help: The roles setColumn accepts in the current state: none with summarized input; with column input response (proportions and equivalence, plus group for two samples), counts (rates, plus group for two rates), before and after (McNemar) or rowVar and colVar (association test).

pickableColumns.help: Per role the columns setColumn accepts, each { key, name }; key is 'instanceId|sheetId|columnId'. Any column with at least 2 values.

eventValueOptions.help: The values setParam accepts for eventValue: the distinct values of the chosen response column, for McNemar of both paired columns together; empty while there is none.

result.help: The test report: figures, notes, decision and, for the association test, the cross table, each figure described individually under keys; null while the inputs are incomplete or invalid (errorMsg gives the reason).

errorMsg.help: The reason there is no result: an input hint while counts or columns are missing, or the refusal (for example a table that is too small or a p0 outside the range); an empty string while a result exists.

Action.key: Identifier of the offered next step; currently only “actionCheckEquivalence” (below a non-significant two-sided two-proportion test), run via checkEquivalence.

equiv.samples: “1 sample” tests whether one proportion is equivalent to p₀; “2 samples” tests whether the difference of two proportions lies within the bounds. Default: 2 samples. The test shares its counts with the one- or two-proportion test.
equiv.symmetric: “Symmetric bounds (±δ)” uses one margin δ for both sides, “Separate bounds” a lower and an upper bound. Default: symmetric.
equiv.delta: Equivalence margin δ in percentage points, a number greater than 0: equivalent means the difference (p − p₀ for one sample) lies between −δ and +δ. The margin is a subject-matter decision, not a statistical one.
equiv.lower: Lower equivalence bound in percentage points, below 0; relative to p₀ for one sample. It must be below the upper bound.
equiv.upper: Upper equivalence bound in percentage points, above 0; relative to p₀ for one sample. It must be above the lower bound.

Params.exposurePerRow: “Exposure per row” for rates from columns: which exposure (time, area, units) belongs to one row of the counts column, a number greater than 0, default 1. The total exposure is the number of rows with a value times this exposure, per group for two rates.
Params.ratePooled: Pooled rate for the two-rate z-test. When checked, the test computes the standard error from the common rate (x₁ + x₂)/(t₁ + t₂); this applies only while the hypothesized difference Δ₀ is 0, otherwise a note appears and the test uses separate estimates. The confidence interval of the difference always stays unpooled. Default: unchecked.
Params.testKind: The test type, chosen in the “Test” section: “1 proportion” tests one proportion against the hypothesized proportion p₀, “2 proportions” compares the proportions of two samples, “Equivalence (proportions)” tests whether a proportion or a difference lies within subject-matter bounds, “McNemar (paired)” compares proportions of the same units before and after, “1 Poisson rate” and “2 Poisson rates” test events per exposure, “Chi-square association” tests whether two categorical variables of a cross table are associated. Default is “2 proportions”; switching keeps all other inputs.
Params.inputMode: The input type in the “Input” section: “Summarized” takes counts entered by hand (events and trials, or the cross table), “Columns” counts them from columns of a data collection. Default is “Summarized”.
Params.alpha: Significance level α, a number strictly between 0 and 1, for example 0.05. H₀ is rejected when the deciding p-value is below α; α also sets the confidence level of the interval, 1 − α in percent, rounded to one decimal.
Params.direction: The alternative hypothesis: “≠ two-sided”, “> greater” or “< less”. For one and two proportions it sets the p-values and the confidence interval; one-sided, the interval extends to 0 or 1 (one proportion) or to −1 or 1 (difference). For the association test it appears only for a 2 × 2 table and affects only Fisher's exact test; Pearson χ² stays two-sided.
Params.p0: Hypothesized proportion p₀ for the one-proportion test, as a number with a point or comma, for example 0.5 (default). It must lie strictly between 0 and 1, otherwise there is no result.
Params.pooled: Pooled estimate of p for the z-test of two proportions. When checked, the test computes the standard error from the common proportion p̄ = (x₁ + x₂)/(n₁ + n₂): SE = √(p̄(1 − p̄)(1/n₁ + 1/n₂)); otherwise from both proportions separately. The confidence interval of the difference always stays unpooled. Default: unchecked.

labels.before: Label of the first time point of the McNemar table, such as “Before” or an inspector's name; shown in hypotheses and figures. Empty means “before”, with column input the column name.
labels.after: Label of the second time point of the McNemar table, such as “After”; shown in hypotheses and figures. Empty means “after”, with column input the column name.

summary.diff0: Hypothesized difference Δ₀ of the rates λ₁ − λ₂ when comparing two rates, default 0. Only at 0 are the conditional exact test and the pooled rate available.
summary.lambda0: Hypothesized rate λ₀ for the one-rate test, events per unit of exposure, a number greater than 0.
summary.t2: Exposure (t) of sample 2 when comparing two rates, a number greater than 0.
summary.t1: Exposure (t) per sample for comparing two rates, rows “Sample 1” and “Sample 2”, a number greater than 0. The sample's rate is events / t.
summary.t: Exposure (t) for the one-rate test: the amount of observation the events refer to (time, area, units), a number greater than 0. The rate is λ̂ = events / t.
summary.x: Events for the one-proportion test: how often the event of interest occurred, a whole number from 0, at most the number of trials. If events and trials are both empty, nothing is computed.
summary.n: Trials (n) for the one-proportion test: the number of observations, a whole number greater than 0. The estimated proportion is p̂ = events / n.
summary.x1: Events per sample when comparing two proportions, rows “Sample 1” and “Sample 2”: how often the event occurred in that sample, a whole number from 0, at most its number of trials.
summary.n1: Trials (n) per sample when comparing two proportions, rows “Sample 1” and “Sample 2”: the number of observations in that sample, a whole number greater than 0. The sample's proportion is events / n.
summary.x2: Events in sample 2 when comparing two proportions, a whole number from 0, at most the trials of sample 2.
summary.n2: Trials (n) in sample 2 when comparing two proportions, a whole number greater than 0.

Params.eventValue: With column input, the value of the response column that counts as an event (“Event =”); for McNemar it applies to both paired columns. The response column needs exactly two distinct values; without a choice, as in Minitab, the last value in natural sort order is used.

Result.decisionParams: Placeholders of the equivalence decision: lower and upper bound (formatted), the unit (% for one sample, pp for two) and α. Equivalence test only.
Result.actions: The next steps below the result: for a non-significant two-sided two-proportion test the “Check with equivalence test” button, because no difference does not mean equivalent. Otherwise the field is missing.
Result.kind: The test type the report was computed for, as chosen in the “Test” section: one proportion, two proportions, equivalence, McNemar, one rate, two rates or chi-square association.
Result.stats: The figure rows of the table under “Results”, different for each test type: counts, proportions, confidence interval, test statistic and p-values; each row is explained individually: hold Alt and click the question mark next to its label.
Result.notes: Notes below the decision: skipped rows with missing values, the unsuitable normal approximation (one proportion), the pooled z-test (two proportions), removed empty rows or columns and the warnings about small expected counts (association test).
Result.decision: The decision against α: “Reject H₀” (reject) when the deciding p-value is below α, otherwise “Do not reject H₀” (keep); for the equivalence test “equivalent” or “not shown” (notEquivalent). The deciding test is the exact binomial test for one proportion, the z-test for two proportions, the exact Poisson test for one rate, the z-test of the difference for two rates, the exact test for McNemar, the TOST for equivalence and Pearson χ² (always two-sided) for the association test. The basis is shown next to the decision.
Result.basisKey: Identifier of the sentence naming the basis of the decision: exact binomial test, z-test, exact Poisson test, z-test of the rate difference, exact McNemar test, TOST or Pearson χ².
Result.table: The cross table of the association test with observed and expected counts and each cell's contribution to χ²; empty for one and two proportions.
Result.noteDetails: The notes as a code with the inserted numbers, in the same order as notes; the numbers are unrounded, for example the share for warnShareBelow5 as a value between 0 and 1.
Result.pValue: The p-value the decision rests on, as a number: exact for one proportion, McNemar and the Poisson rate, z-test for two proportions and two rates, TOST for equivalence, Pearson chi-square for the association test. Null when it cannot be computed.
Result.ci: The confidence interval as [lower, upper] in the unit of the statistic, unrounded; a non-finite bound is null. Null for the association test, which has no interval. For equivalence it is the (1 − 2α) TOST interval. The number is always a fraction or rate, never percent.

Stat.key: Identifier of the figure row, unique within one test type; the same identifier can mean different things in different test types.
Stat.labelKey: Identifier of the row's label text; for Fisher's exact test of a 2 × 2 table in the association test there is one per direction (two-sided, one-sided greater, one-sided less); when comparing two proportions the Fisher row always carries the same label without a direction, even for a one-sided alternative.
Stat.params: Placeholders of the label: the confidence level in percent, the group name or the degrees of freedom; missing for rows without placeholders.
Stat.value: The value as formatted text, as in the table: four decimals, χ², G² and Yates with three, p-values below 0.0001 as “< 0.0001”, counts as “x / n”, confidence intervals as lower and upper bound; decimal point in both languages, “–” for a value that cannot be computed.
Stat.num: The statistic as a number; null for counts and intervals — the interval is under ci. Shares and rates are given as fractions, never percent.

Note.key: Identifier of the note text shown below the decision.
Note.params: Placeholders of the note: the number of skipped rows, the names of removed rows or columns, or the rounded percentage of cells with an expected count below 5; missing for notes without placeholders.

Warning.code: The id of the note, equal to the text key.
Warning.values: The numbers behind the notice, by name, unrounded; shares as a value between 0 and 1; not computable is null.

CrossTable.cols: The column levels of the cross table; columns without observations are removed.
CrossTable.rows: The rows of the cross table; rows without observations are removed.

CrossRow.name: The row level, on the left of the cross table.
CrossRow.cells: The cells of the row, one per column level.

CrossCell.obs: Observed count of the cell, the top number.
CrossCell.exp: Expected count under independence: row total · column total / grand total, with two decimals.
CrossCell.contrib: Each cell shows three numbers: the observed count o, the count expected under independence e = row total · column total / grand total, and the contribution (o − e)²/e to Pearson χ². Large contributions show where the association lies.

equiv.counts: Events and trials of the sample as “x / n”.
equiv.counts1: Events and trials of the first group as “x / n”.
equiv.counts2: Events and trials of the second group as “x / n”.
equiv.estimate: The estimate: for one sample the proportion p̂ in percent, for two the difference p̂₁ − p̂₂ in percentage points.
equiv.ci: Confidence interval at level 1 − 2α, as it belongs to two one-sided tests at level α. If it lies entirely within the bounds, the proportions are equivalent.
equiv.bounds: The equivalence bounds in the unit of the estimate; for one sample p₀ plus the bounds, clipped to 0 to 100 %.
equiv.pLower: p-value of the one-sided test against the lower bound.
equiv.pUpper: p-value of the one-sided test against the upper bound.
equiv.pValue: p-value of the TOST, the larger of the two one-sided p-values. Equivalent when it is below α.

mcnemar.discordant: The discordant pairs as “b / c”: b changes from event to no event, c from no event to event. Only they contribute to the test.
mcnemar.pBefore: Proportion of pairs with the event at the first time point.
mcnemar.pAfter: Proportion of pairs with the event at the second time point.
mcnemar.diff: Difference of the proportions after − before.
mcnemar.ci: Wald confidence interval of the paired difference, level 1 − α; one-sided for a directional alternative with −1 or 1 as the open bound.
mcnemar.pExact: p-value of the exact McNemar test, the binomial test of c among b + c pairs with p = 0.5, in the chosen direction. Basis of the decision.
mcnemar.chi2: McNemar χ² = (b − c)² / (b + c) without continuity correction; two-sided only.
mcnemar.pChi2: p-value of McNemar χ² with one degree of freedom, for information only.
mcnemar.chi2Cc: McNemar χ² with continuity correction: (|b − c| − 1)² / (b + c); two-sided only.
mcnemar.pChi2Cc: p-value of the corrected χ², for information only.

rate2.rate1: Rate of the first group λ̂₁ = x₁ / t₁; group name from the group column, “1” with summarized input.
rate2.rate2: Rate of the second group λ̂₂ = x₂ / t₂.
rate2.diff: Difference of the rates λ̂₁ − λ̂₂.
rate2.ci: Confidence interval of the difference from the normal approximation with separate standard error, level 1 − α, always unpooled.
rate2.z: Statistic z = (λ̂₁ − λ̂₂ − Δ₀) / SE; SE from the pooled rate when checked and Δ₀ = 0, otherwise separate.
rate2.pValue: p-value of the z-test in the chosen direction. Basis of the decision.
rate2.pExactCond: p-value of the conditional exact test: given the total x₁ + x₂, x₁ is binomial with p = t₁/(t₁ + t₂). Only for Δ₀ = 0 and at least one event, for information.
rate2.ratio: Rate ratio λ̂₁ / λ̂₂; missing when the second group has no event.
rate2.ratioCi: Exact confidence interval of the rate ratio from the Clopper-Pearson interval of the conditional binomial proportion, level 1 − α.

rate1.rate: Estimated rate λ̂ = x / t, events per unit of exposure.
rate1.ci: Exact Garwood confidence interval from chi-square quantiles, level 1 − α; one-sided for a directional alternative.
rate1.pExact: p-value of the exact Poisson test in the chosen direction, two-sided twice the smaller tail, at most 1. Basis of the decision.
rate1.pNormal: p-value of the normal approximation, for information only; suitable from λ₀·t ≥ 5, otherwise a note appears.

one.counts: Events and trials of the sample as “x / n”.
one.ci: Exact Clopper-Pearson confidence interval from beta distribution quantiles, level 1 − α. One-sided for a directional alternative, the open side extending to 0 or 1; for x = 0 the lower bound is 0, for x = n the upper bound is 1.
one.pExact: p-value of the exact binomial test: for “> greater” P(X ≥ x), for “< less” P(X ≤ x), two-sided twice the smaller tail, at most 1. Basis of the decision: H₀ is rejected when it is below α.
one.z: Test statistic of the normal approximation z = (p̂ − p₀) / √(p₀(1 − p₀)/n).
one.pNormal: p-value of the normal approximation from z in the chosen direction, for information only. Suitable only when n·p₀ ≥ 5, n·(1 − p₀) ≥ 5 and 0 < x < n; otherwise a note appears and the exact test applies.

two.counts1: Events and trials of the first group as “x / n”; group name from the group column, “1” with summarized input.
two.counts2: Events and trials of the second group as “x / n”; group name from the group column, “2” with summarized input.
two.p1: Proportion of the first group p₁ = x₁ / n₁.
two.p2: Proportion of the second group p₂ = x₂ / n₂.
two.diff: Difference of the proportions p₁ − p₂.
two.ci: Wald confidence interval of the difference: p₁ − p₂ ± z₁₋α/₂ · SE at level 1 − α, the standard error always unpooled, even when the test is pooled. One-sided for a directional alternative, with −1 or 1 as the open bound.
two.z: Test statistic z = (p₁ − p₂) / SE; SE pooled or separate, depending on the “Use pooled estimate of p for the test” checkbox. If SE is 0, “–” is shown.
two.pValue: p-value of the z-test in the chosen direction. Basis of the decision: H₀ is rejected when it is below α.
two.pFisher: p-value of Fisher's exact test of the 2 × 2 table of events and non-events in both groups, in the chosen direction; two-sided, the sum over all tables at most as likely as the observed one. For information only.

assoc.pearson: Pearson χ² = Σ (o − e)²/e over all cells, with DF = (rows − 1)·(columns − 1). Unreliable when an expected count is below 1 or more than 20 % are below 5; a warning then appears.
assoc.pPearson: p-value of Pearson χ², always two-sided. Basis of the decision: H₀, independence, is rejected when it is below α.
assoc.lr: Likelihood ratio G² = 2 · Σ o · ln(o/e) over the cells with observations, with the same DF as Pearson χ².
assoc.pLR: p-value of the likelihood ratio G², for information only.
assoc.yates: χ² with Yates correction, only for a 2 × 2 table: Σ max(0, |o − e| − 0.5)²/e.
assoc.pYates: p-value of the Yates-corrected χ² with one degree of freedom, only for a 2 × 2 table.
assoc.pFisher: p-value of Fisher's exact test, only for a 2 × 2 table. It is the only figure that follows the chosen alternative hypothesis; with a one-sided alternative the label names the direction.

sample-size.name: Sample Size
sample-size.description: Calculate the required sample size for variance and mean tests
sample-size.whenToUse: When you need to know how many observations a test requires: computes the required sample size for variance tests (chi-square, F) and mean tests (one- and two-sample t) from the effect to detect, the significance level and the target power.

read.help: Returns the ten inputs, the keys valid in the current state and the result. result is null while the inputs are incomplete or not positive numbers.

params.options: Optional; this module holds no bulk data.

setParam.help: Sets one input; the calculation reruns.

params.key: Which option; each is described individually under keys, the ones allowed in the current state are listed in activeParams. Any other value is an error.
params.value: The value; type and allowed range per key are given under keys. sigma0, sigmaAlt, ratio, delta, sigma as text containing a number; '' clears the value.

runAnalysis.help: Calculates the required sample size from the current inputs. While the inputs are incomplete or not positive numbers result stays null.

category.help: Which kind of test the sample size is for: 'variance' or 'mean'.

alpha.help: The significance level as a number; null until it is taken from the settings.

power.help: The target power (1 − β) as a number; null until it is taken from the settings.

sigma0.help: Hypothesized standard deviation σ₀ as entered; applies to variance with one sample.

sigmaAlt.help: Expected standard deviation σ₁ as entered; applies to variance with one sample.

ratio.help: Variance ratio σ²₁/σ²₂ as entered; applies to variance with two samples.

delta.help: Mean difference Δ to detect, as entered; applies to mean tests.

sigma.help: Standard deviation σ, as entered; applies to mean tests.

activeParams.help: The keys setParam accepts in the current state.

result.help: The required sample size, each figure described individually under keys; null while an effect input is missing or not positive.

Params.category: The test category, buttons “σ² Variances” and “μ Means”: variances (variance) plan a test on the spread, means (mean) a t-test on the location. The choice decides which effect inputs apply.
Params.testType: The test type, buttons “1-Sample” and “2-Sample”: one compares one sample with a target value, two compares two equally sized groups with each other. With two samples the computed size is per group.
Params.direction: The direction, field “Direction”: “Two-sided” detects a deviation in either direction, “Greater” and “Less” only one in that direction. A one-sided test needs fewer observations only when it points in the direction of the effect. For means Δ always counts as a positive, upward deviation; “Less” therefore never reaches the target power and ends at the upper limit of 5000. For variances the direction must match the effect: “Greater” when σ₁ is above σ₀ or the ratio above 1, “Less” when below; otherwise the search also ends at 5000.
Params.alpha: The significance level α, the accepted probability of reporting an effect that does not exist; a number from 0.0001 to 0.5. Prefilled from the confidence in the settings (95% gives 0.05). A smaller α requires more observations.
Params.power: The target power 1 − β, label “Target Power (1 − β)”: the probability of actually detecting an existing effect of the given size; a number from 0.5 to 0.9999, prefilled from the settings (typically 0.8). Higher power requires more observations.
Params.sigma0: The hypothesized standard deviation σ₀, label “Hypothesized Std. (σ₀)”: the spread assumed by the hypothesis H₀ under test, as text containing a positive number. Only for variances with one sample; the effect is the ratio σ₁² / σ₀².
Params.sigmaAlt: The expected standard deviation σ₁, label “Expected Std. (σ₁)”: the spread whose deviation from σ₀ the test should detect, as text containing a positive number. Only for variances with one sample; the closer σ₁ is to σ₀, the more observations are needed.
Params.ratio: The variance ratio σ²₁ / σ²₂, label “Variance Ratio (σ²₁ / σ²₂)”: the factor by which the variances of the two groups should differ, as text containing a positive number. Only for variances with two samples; a ratio close to 1 requires very many observations.
Params.delta: The mean difference Δ to detect, label “Difference (Δ)”, as text containing a positive number in the unit of the measurements: with one sample the distance to the target, with two the distance between the group means. Only for means; together with σ it gives the effect size Cohen's d = Δ / σ.
Params.sigma: The standard deviation σ of the measurements, label “Std. Dev. (σ)”, as text containing a positive number; with two samples it applies to both groups. Only for means; a larger σ makes the same difference harder to detect.

Result.nRequired: The required sample size n, tile “Required n” (with two samples “per group”): the smallest n from 4 on at which the power reaches the target power. The search runs up to 5000. If the target power is reached only at 5000 or not at all, this is 5000 and the tile shows “> 5,000” (German “> 5.000”) instead of the number; the summary above the tiles names the same value. The effect is then hardly detectable.
Result.totalN: The total size, tile “Total n”: with two samples n per group times two, with one sample equal to n. The tile appears only with two samples; from an n of 5000 on it shows “> 10,000” (German “> 10.000”).
Result.alpha: The significance level α used in the calculation, tile “α”; equal to the input.
Result.power: The target power 1 − β used in the calculation, as a fraction; the tile “Target Power” shows it as a percentage rounded to whole numbers. The size n reaches at least this power unless it sits at the upper limit of 5000, where the search ends.
Result.effectLabel: The name of the effect size as the tile shows it: “Variance Ratio” for variance tests, “Cohen's d” for mean tests.
Result.effectValue: The effect size the test should detect; the tile shows it with three decimals. Variances, one sample: σ₁² / σ₀². Variances, two samples: the entered ratio σ²₁ / σ²₂. Means: Cohen's d = Δ / σ.
Result.algoId: The procedure whose power was calculated; the interface uses it to link the Algorithm Lab. chi-square-variance: χ² test of one variance with n − 1 degrees of freedom. f-test: F-test of two variances with n − 1 degrees of freedom each. one-sample-t-test: t-test with noncentrality Δ · √n / σ and n − 1 degrees of freedom. two-sample-t-test: t-test with noncentrality Δ / (σ · √(2/n)) and 2n − 2 degrees of freedom.

sample-size.placeholderText: Enter parameters on the left and run the calculation.
sample-size.resultSummary: With n = {n}, a power of {power}% is achieved at α = {alpha}.
sample-size.nOverflow: The required sample size reaches or exceeds 5,000 — the effect is very difficult to detect with these parameters.
sample-size.errRatio: Please enter a valid variance ratio > 0.
sample-size.errSigma0: Please enter a valid hypothesized standard deviation > 0.
sample-size.errSigmaAlt: Please enter a valid expected standard deviation > 0.
sample-size.errSigma: Please enter a valid standard deviation > 0.

random-generator.whenToUse: When random data from a known distribution or from weighted categories is needed — for practice, simulations or test data — reproducible through the seed.

read.help: Returns the distribution, its parameters, sample size and seed, the categories, the selectable sets and a summary of the generated values. generated is null while there are no values; read the values themselves from the worksheet after toWorksheet.

params.options: Optional; this module holds no bulk data.

selectDistribution.help: Chooses the distribution and generates values at once with the sample size and seed that apply to it.

params.key: One of the distributions in distributions, attributive included; any other value is an error.

setDistParam.help: Sets one parameter of the chosen distribution; the formula above the fields shows where it enters, the allowed range is given below the field. Values outside the range are rejected, not clamped. The values are generated again at once.

params.id: One of the parameters in activeDistParams, for example mu or sigma. Which apply depends on the distribution.
params.value: A number within min to max from activeDistParams; numbers given as text are accepted.

setParam.help: Sets the sample size or the seed and generates again at once. Values outside the range are rejected, not clamped.

params.key: Which option; each is described individually under keys, the ones allowed in the current state are listed in activeParams. Any other value is an error.
params.value: The value; type and allowed range per key are given under keys.

addAttribute.help: Adds an attribute (a category) to the attributive distribution, with an empty name and weight 1, and generates again. Categories without a name are skipped when generating. The agent receives the id of the category.

removeAttribute.help: Removes a category of the attributive distribution and generates again.

params.attrId: The id of a category from attributes; any other id is an error.

setAttribute.help: Sets the name or the weight of a category of the attributive distribution and generates again. Categories with an empty name or a weight of 0 or less are skipped when generating.

params.attrId: The id of a category from attributes, or the one addAttribute returned.
params.key: Which field; each is described individually under keys. Any other value is an error.
params.value: The value; type and allowed range per key are given under keys.

generate.help: Generates the values with the current inputs. Without a chosen distribution nothing happens; a failure of the distribution is reported in errorMsg, not as a rejection.

toWorksheet.help: Sends the generated values to a new worksheet, into an existing empty column or as a new column to an existing sheet. If there are no values, nothing is sent. The agent receives the receiving worksheet; without values it receives none.

params.target: null for a new worksheet, otherwise a column reference { instanceId, sheetId, columnId } from targetColumns; columnId '__new__' appends a new column to the sheet.

currentDist.help: The chosen distribution, one of the keys in distributions, or null.

distributions.help: All distributions selectDistribution accepts, attributive included.

params.help: The parameters of the chosen continuous or discrete distribution as numbers, by id.

activeDistParams.help: The parameters setDistParam accepts in the chosen distribution, each with id, bounds (null without a bound) and default.

activeParams.help: The keys setParam accepts in the current state; empty without a chosen distribution.

count.help: Sample size of a continuous or discrete distribution.

seed.help: Random seed of a continuous or discrete distribution.

attributes.help: The categories of the attributive distribution, each with id, name and weight.

attrCount.help: Sample size of the attributive distribution.

attrSeed.help: Random seed of the attributive distribution.

generated.help: Summary of the generated values, each item described individually under keys; null while no values are generated. The cards show the statistics with four decimals, magnitudes from 10⁶ or below 0.001 in exponential notation.

targetColumns.help: The targets toWorksheet accepts, each { key, name }; key is 'instanceId|sheetId|columnId'. Per sheet with an empty column it lists its empty columns followed by an entry with columnId '__new__' (name is the sheet name) that appends a new column. A null target creates a new worksheet.

errorMsg.help: The message when the distribution could not produce values, otherwise empty.

Params.count: Count (n): the sample size for a continuous or discrete distribution, a whole number from 1 to 100,000. A change generates the values again at once.
Params.seed: Seed: the starting value of the random generator for a continuous or discrete distribution. The same seed gives the same values, so the sample is reproducible. Any whole number is allowed, 0 included; an empty field becomes 42. A change generates the values again at once.
Params.attrCount: Count (n): the sample size for the attributive distribution, a whole number from 1 to 100,000. A change generates the values again at once.
Params.attrSeed: Seed: the starting value of the random generator for the attributive distribution. The same seed gives the same values, so the sample is reproducible. Any whole number is allowed, 0 included; an empty field becomes 42. A change generates the values again at once.

AttributeFields.name: Attribute: the name of the category. It may be empty; categories without a name are skipped when generating.
AttributeFields.weight: Weight of the category, a number from 0. The share of a category is its weight divided by the sum of all weights; the column "Share" shows it in percent. A category with weight 0 is skipped when generating.

Generated.n: n: the number of generated values, equal to the set count (n).
Generated.mean: Mean x̄ = Σx / n, the sum of the generated values divided by their count. Only for continuous and discrete distributions.
Generated.sd: Std.Dev. s = √(Σ(x − x̄)² / (n − 1)), the sample spread of the generated values with denominator n − 1. Not defined for a single drawn value: the result is then empty. Only for continuous and discrete distributions.
Generated.median: Median: the middle of the generated values sorted ascending, for an even count the mean of the two middle ones. Only for continuous and discrete distributions.
Generated.min: Min: the smallest of the generated values. Only for continuous and discrete distributions.
Generated.max: Max: the largest of the generated values. Only for continuous and discrete distributions.
Generated.skewness: Skewness g₁ = m₃ / m₂^1.5 with the central moments m₂ = Σ(x − x̄)² / n and m₃ = Σ(x − x̄)³ / n (denominator n, not corrected). Positive: the long tail is on the right, negative: on the left; 0 for symmetric values. Only for continuous and discrete distributions.
Generated.kurtosis: Kurtosis as excess: m₄ / m₂² − 3 with m₂ = Σ(x − x̄)² / n and m₄ = Σ(x − x̄)⁴ / n (denominator n, not corrected). 0 matches the normal distribution, positive means more peaked with heavy tails, negative flatter. Only for continuous and discrete distributions.
Generated.frequency: The frequency per category, sorted descending by count; each entry gives name and count. The card "Categories" counts the entries, the card "Most frequent" names the first one. Only for the attributive distribution.

normal.mu: Mean (μ): the location of the distribution, around which the values scatter. Allowed: any number; default 0.
normal.sigma: Std. Dev. (σ): the scale, the spread of the values around the location. Allowed: number from 0.0001; default 1.
normal.epsilon: Skewness (ε): the asymmetry: 0 gives symmetric values, positive values make the distribution right-skewed (long right tail), negative values left-skewed. Allowed: any number; default 0.
normal.delta: Tailweight (δ): how heavy the tails are: 1 gives the normal distribution, values below 1 make the tails heavier, values above 1 lighter. Allowed: number from 0.01; default 1.

chisquare.k: Degrees of freedom (k): they set the shape of the chi-square distribution; the larger, the more symmetric. Allowed: number from 1, whole numbers are usual; default 5.

f_dist.d1: Degrees of freedom d₁: the number of degrees of freedom in the numerator of the F distribution. Allowed: number from 1, whole numbers are usual; default 5.
f_dist.d2: Degrees of freedom d₂: the number of degrees of freedom in the denominator of the F distribution. Allowed: number from 1, whole numbers are usual; default 10.

t_dist.nu: Degrees of freedom (ν): they set the shape of the t distribution; the larger, the closer it is to the normal distribution. Allowed: number from 1, whole numbers are usual; default 10.

uniform.a: Lower bound (a): the lower bound, below which no values occur. Allowed: any number; default 0.
uniform.b: Upper bound (b): the upper bound, above which no values occur; it should exceed the lower bound, otherwise the values lie reversed between b and a. Allowed: any number; default 1.

beta.alpha: Shape α: the first shape of the beta distribution; together with β it decides whether the values between 0 and 1 lie more to the left or to the right. Allowed: number from 0.01; default 2.
beta.beta: Shape β: the second shape of the beta distribution; together with α it decides whether the values between 0 and 1 lie more to the left or to the right. Allowed: number from 0.01; default 5.

cauchy.x0: Location (x₀): the location, the center of the Cauchy distribution (its median). Allowed: any number; default 0.
cauchy.gamma: Scale (γ): the scale, the width of the Cauchy distribution. Allowed: number from 0.0001; default 1.

exponential.lambda: Rate (λ): the rate: how many events occur per unit; the mean of the values is 1/λ. Allowed: number from 0.0001; default 1.

gamma_dist.alpha: Shape (α): the shape of the gamma distribution; 1 gives the exponential distribution, larger values make it more symmetric. Allowed: number from 0.01; default 2.
gamma_dist.beta: Scale (β): the scale of the gamma distribution, by which all values are stretched. Allowed: number from 0.0001; default 1.

laplace.mu: Location (μ): the location, the center of the Laplace distribution. Allowed: any number; default 0.
laplace.b: Scale (b): the scale, the width of the Laplace distribution. Allowed: number from 0.0001; default 1.

gumbel_max.mu: Location (μ): the location of the Gumbel distribution for maxima (its mode). Allowed: any number; default 0.
gumbel_max.beta: Scale (β): the scale, the width of the Gumbel distribution for maxima. Allowed: number from 0.0001; default 1.

logistic.mu: Location (μ): the location, the center of the logistic distribution. Allowed: any number; default 0.
logistic.s: Scale (s): the scale, the width of the logistic distribution. Allowed: number from 0.0001; default 1.

loglogistic.alpha: Scale (α): the scale of the log-logistic distribution, which is also its median. Allowed: number from 0.0001; default 1.
loglogistic.beta: Shape (β): the shape of the log-logistic distribution; the larger, the more tightly the values lie around the scale. Allowed: number from 0.0001; default 1.

lognormal.mu: Log-Mean (μ): the mean of the logarithms of the values (not of the values themselves). Allowed: any number; default 0.
lognormal.sigma: Log-Std.Dev. (σ): the standard deviation of the logarithms of the values (not of the values themselves). Allowed: number from 0.0001; default 1.

gumbel_min.mu: Location (μ): the location of the Gumbel distribution for minima (its mode). Allowed: any number; default 0.
gumbel_min.beta: Scale (β): the scale, the width of the Gumbel distribution for minima. Allowed: number from 0.0001; default 1.

triangular.a: Minimum (a): the minimum, the smallest possible value. Allowed: any number; default 0.
triangular.c: Mode (c): the mode, the most frequent value; it should lie between the minimum and the maximum. Allowed: any number; default 0.5.
triangular.b: Maximum (b): the maximum, the largest possible value; it should exceed the minimum. Allowed: any number; default 1.

weibull.alpha: Shape (α): the shape of the Weibull distribution; 1 gives the exponential distribution, above 1 the failure rate rises over time. Allowed: number from 0.0001; default 1.5.
weibull.beta: Scale (β): the scale of the Weibull distribution (characteristic life: 63.2 % of the values lie below it). Allowed: number from 0.0001; default 1.

bernoulli.p: Success prob. (p): the probability that a trial succeeds and yields 1; otherwise 0 results. Allowed: number from 0 to 1; default 0.5.

binomial.n: Trials (n): how often the trial is repeated for each generated value; the value counts the successes. Allowed: number from 1, whole numbers are usual; default 10.
binomial.p: Success prob. (p): the probability that a single trial succeeds. Allowed: number from 0 to 1; default 0.5.

geometric.p: Success prob. (p): the probability that a single trial succeeds; the value counts the failures before the first success. Allowed: number from 0.0001 to 1; default 0.3.

negbinomial.r: Successes (r): how many successes are waited for; the value counts the failures up to then. Allowed: number from 1, whole numbers are usual; default 5.
negbinomial.p: Success prob. (p): the probability that a single trial succeeds. Allowed: number from 0.0001 to 1; default 0.5.

hypergeometric.N: Population size (N): the number of all elements drawn from without replacement. Allowed: number from 1, whole numbers are usual; default 100.
hypergeometric.K: Success states (K): how many of the N elements are successes; it should be at most as large as N. Allowed: number from 0, whole numbers are usual; default 30.
hypergeometric.n: Sample size (n): how many elements are drawn for each generated value; it should be at most as large as N, and the value counts the successes among them. Allowed: number from 1, whole numbers are usual; default 10.

integer.a: Minimum (a): the smallest whole number that can occur; it should not be larger than the maximum. Allowed: any number, decimals are rounded down; default 1.
integer.b: Maximum (b): the largest whole number that can occur; it should not be smaller than the minimum. Allowed: any number, decimals are rounded down; default 6.

poisson.lambda: Rate (λ): the mean number of events per unit; it is both the mean and the variance of the values. Allowed: number from 0.01; default 5.

mvnormal.mu1: Mean μ₁: the location of the first component of the two-dimensional normal distribution; it determines the generated values. Allowed: any number; default 0.
mvnormal.mu2: Mean μ₂: the location of the second component; the generated column holds only the first component, so μ₂ does not currently change it. Allowed: any number; default 0.
mvnormal.sigma1: Std.Dev. σ₁: the spread of the first component around its mean μ₁. Allowed: number from 0.0001; default 1.
mvnormal.sigma2: Std.Dev. σ₂: the spread of the second component around its mean μ₂; the generated column holds only the first component, so σ₂ does not currently change it. Allowed: number from 0.0001; default 1.
mvnormal.rho: Correlation ρ: how strongly the two components are related (-1 opposite, 0 independent, 1 in step); the generated column holds only the first component, so ρ does not currently change it. Allowed: number from -0.999 to 0.999; default 0.5.

FrequencyRow.name: The name of the category.
FrequencyRow.count: How often the category occurs among the generated values.
FrequencyRow.share: The share of the category among all generated values, as a number from 0 to 1 (count divided by the number of values); the display shows it as a percentage.

random-generator.errGenerate: The values could not be generated: {message}
random-generator.name: Random Generator
random-generator.description: Generate reproducible samples from statistical distributions
random-generator.selectDistribution: Select a distribution on the left to get started.

model-data-generator.whenToUse: When synthetic data from a known regression model is needed — to practise DOE analysis and regression, or to test methods against a known “true” model — with factors, coefficients, noise and a seed for reproducible results.

read.help: Returns the factors and terms with their indices, the intercept, the response name, the sampling method, sample size, noise, seed and a summary of the generated values. generated is null until data exists; read the rows themselves from the worksheet after toWorksheet.

params.options: Optional; this module holds no bulk data.

addFactor.help: Appends a factor with a default name and the range 0 to 100. The terms are rebuilt and all coefficients reset to 0, and a generated result is discarded. The agent receives the index of the new factor.

removeFactor.help: Removes a factor. The terms are rebuilt and all coefficients reset to 0, and a generated result is discarded. The last factor stays: the action then returns false and changes nothing.

params.index: The index of a factor from factors; any other value is an error.

setFactor.help: Sets the name or a range limit of a factor; a generated result is discarded. The coefficients are kept. Invalid values are rejected.

params.index: The index of a factor from factors; any other value is an error.
params.key: Which field; each is described individually under keys. Any other value is an error.
params.value: The value; type and permitted range are given per key under keys.

setBeta.help: Sets the coefficient of a term. An already generated result stays until the next generate and keeps the old values until then.

params.index: The index of a term from terms; any other value is an error.
params.value: A finite number; numbers given as text are accepted.

setIntercept.help: Sets the intercept β₀ of the model equation. An already generated result stays until the next generate.

params.value: A finite number; numbers given as text are accepted.

setYName.help: Sets the name of the response Y; it appears in the equation, the table and the export. It must not be empty and must not name a factor, since the Y column would otherwise overwrite a factor column. An already generated result stays until the next generate.

params.value: The name as text, not empty and not a factor name.

setSamplingMethod.help: Chooses the sampling method: random (Monte Carlo), Latin Hypercube (LHS) or full factorial. Takes effect on the next generate.

params.value: One of the methods in samplingMethods; any other value is an error.

setSampleSize.help: Sets the number of rows. With the full factorial method the number of levels is fixed (3 levels up to 4 factors, otherwise 2); the number only sets how often each level combination is repeated (n divided by the number of combinations, rounded, at least 1), so the row count usually differs from it. Takes effect on the next generate. Values outside the range are rejected, not clamped.

params.value: An integer from 10 to 100000; numbers given as text are accepted.

setNoiseStd.help: Sets the standard deviation σε of the normally distributed noise added to the modelled Y value. 0 produces values without noise. Takes effect on the next generate.

params.value: A number from 0; numbers given as text are accepted.

setSeed.help: Sets the seed, the starting value of the random generator. The same seed with the same settings gives the same data. Takes effect on the next generate.

params.value: An integer; numbers given as text are accepted.

generate.help: Generates the data with the current settings and shows it in the preview. The agent receives the summary of the Y values, the same as generated; it reads the rows from the worksheet after toWorksheet.

toWorksheet.help: Opens the generated data in a new worksheet and switches to it. If no data exists yet, it generates first. The agent receives the id of the new worksheet.

factors.help: The factors, each with index, name, min and max. The index addresses the factor in setFactor and removeFactor.

terms.help: All terms of the model — main effects and interactions — each with index, label, order and beta, zeros included. The index addresses the term in setBeta. The list changes with the number of factors.

intercept.help: The intercept β₀ of the model equation.

yName.help: Name of the response Y, also the column name of the generated data.

samplingMethod.help: The chosen sampling method, one of the methods in samplingMethods.

sampleSize.help: The requested number of rows; with the full factorial method only a guide for the repetitions per level combination.

noiseStd.help: Standard deviation σε of the noise added to the modelled Y value.

seed.help: Seed, the starting value of the random generator; the same seed gives the same data.

maxOrder.help: The upper limit of the interaction order among the terms; with fewer factors the terms stop at the factor count. It is fixed and cannot be changed.

generated.help: Summary of the generated Y values, each item described individually under keys; null until data exists. It is computed on generate. addFactor, removeFactor and setFactor discard it. The other setters — setBeta, setIntercept, setYName, setSamplingMethod, setSampleSize, setNoiseStd, setSeed — leave it in place until the next generate. The cards show the figures with four decimals, magnitudes from 10⁶ or below 0.001 in exponential notation.

FactorFields.name: Name of the factor, also the column name of the data. It must not be empty and must not equal another factor or the response Y.
FactorFields.min: Lower limit of the factor range, a number. It must not exceed the upper limit.
FactorFields.max: Upper limit of the factor range, a number. It must not be below the lower limit.

Generated.n: N: the number of generated rows.
Generated.mean: Mean of the generated Y values.
Generated.sd: Standard deviation of the generated Y values.
Generated.min: Min: the smallest generated Y value.
Generated.max: Max: the largest generated Y value.
